Quick one — during our latest April payouts several fee lines that are ordinarily retained by Redwood were reallocated to our vendor line (Marketplace Fee) and ended up showing on the vendor-facing invoice net value. We’re trying to close month-end and this has a P&L impact. If possible we’d like a proposed short action plan + timeline.

Hi all — looping in finance policy and ops notes so we have a single playbook here. TL;DR: we can remediate with a credit memo + reissued invoice net of fees once we validate MerchantCo’s GST registration; reverse-charge is not applicable in AU — that mechanism is EU-specific.

Policy & action plan (finance):
- Validation: run the GST registration check (attach certificate, confirm ABN/GST number). Finance will record validation result in HubSpot (link below).
- Credit Memo: if validation succeeds we will raise a credit memo for the impacted payout lines and reissue a corrected vendor invoice. Use credit_memo_template.xlsx to build the adjustment.
- Timing: assuming we have the certificate and confirmation today, finance can issue credit memos within 2 business days and the corrected invoice the next day.
- Reconciliation: we’ll tag the adjustment with internal code MC-GST-ADJ-04 and notify MerchantCo’s AP automatically.

Notes / constraints:
- Reverse-charge: only applies inside EU/EEA where the recipient accounts for VAT. For APAC GST we need the vendor’s local GST registration and the invoices must be issued net by the marketplace if the vendor requests it and the regional rules allow.
- Records: we must keep the registration evidence on file for 5 years for audit.

Links & templates: https://app.hubspot.com/records/MC-2026-0931 (merchant record)
Attachment: credit_memo_template.xlsx
